search_context.feature_task: mcp-bpmn-99x BPMN sequence-flow condition/default-flow serialization, schema-aware moddle import round-trip, and persistent-state invariants

critical_patterns.summary: docs/solutions/ is absent in this checkout, so there is no critical-patterns file to apply.

current_repository_evidence.summary: The current executable specification separates labels from conditions, parses expressions through bpmn-moddle, preserves metacharacters/language/type across reopen and save, resolves source.default to the sequence-flow object, and rejects invalid conditional/default combinations without state mutation.
The retained-moddle round-trip tests require unrelated conditions, extension content, semantic references, labels, bounds, and waypoints to survive targeted mutations and reopen.

Persistence tests define the state invariant: serialize and atomically save a cloned working document before publishing it in memory; serialization or write failure must leave the model, XML, and prior file unchanged, and concurrent mutations must not diverge from disk.

recommendations: No repository-documented institutional learnings are available; treat the focused condition/default-flow, import-roundtrip, and persistence tests as the present executable contract for this review.

If this behavior is accepted, record the key invariants in docs/solutions/: conditions are semantic sequence-flow expressions rather than labels; defaults are source-node references and cannot be conditional; retained moddle content must survive typed mutations; and state becomes visible only after successful schema serialization and atomic persistence.
